# Validation against Monte Carlo

radot organ doses are compared with full Monte Carlo simulations performed with [OpenGATE](https://github.com/OpenGATE/opengate) on a patient CT.

## Setup

- **Geometry**: CT of one patient (p142), cropped and resampled to 4 mm. Liver volume 1317 mL, mass 1424 g (from CT density).
- **Activity**: uniform in the liver, 1 MBq at t = 0.
- **OpenGATE**: mean dose rate in the organ at t = 0, integrated with a mono-exponential clearance of effective half-life T<sub>eff</sub>: D = Ḋ(0) · T<sub>eff</sub> / ln 2.
- **radot**: same activity, same organ mass and the same T<sub>eff</sub>. Organ-level methods use the OpenDose ICRP-110 adult male S-values, scaled to the patient organ mass.
- **GATE stat. unc.**: statistical uncertainty (one standard deviation) of the organ mean dose rate, estimated from the voxel uncertainty maps, taking into account that one history deposits in several voxels (mean β range for electrons, mean organ chord for photons). Checked with 20 independent Lu-177 simulations: liver 0.13 % measured vs 0.13 % estimated, right kidney 1.06 % vs 0.94 %; for the 9 organs, the estimate is 0.7 to 1.3 times the measured value.
- **Difference**: (radot − GATE) / GATE.
- **Expected**: acceptance range for |difference| asserted in `validation/opengate/test_opengate.py`.

Cross-doses are about 100 times lower than self-doses and are due to photons. They depend on the position of the organs and the tissue between them, which differ between the reference phantom (used for the S-values) and the patient: radot is higher than GATE for most organs of this patient, by tens of percent and more. The organ-level S-value methods give the order of magnitude of a cross-dose, not a patient-specific value. The CT is cropped around the liver (34 cm along the body axis): a simulation on the full-body CT changes the cross-doses by less than 10 % (left kidney +9 %, heart +3 %, the others within the statistical uncertainty). With t = T<sub>eff</sub> / 2, Hänscheid 2018 is identical to Madsen 2018.

## What this validates

- The **absorbed dose per decay**: S-values, organ mass scaling, and the energy deposited locally by the LDM, including decay chains (Ac-225 cascade).
- The handling of several radionuclides with very different emissions (β⁻ with and without γ, α chain).

## What this does not validate

- **Kinetics**: T<sub>eff</sub> is the same for radot and GATE, so the time-integration models (single-time-point assumptions, curve fitting) are not tested here.
- **Non-uniform activity**: the activity is uniform in the liver; real SPECT distributions are not yet compared.
- **Other source organs and patients**: one patient, one source organ (liver).
- **Image-based steps**: SPECT quantification, segmentation and registration are outside the scope of this comparison.

## How the reference was produced

The scripts and configurations are in [`validation/opengate/`](https://github.com/dsarrut/radot/tree/main/validation/opengate); the images and OpenGATE outputs are on Zenodo: [doi:10.5281/zenodo.23696023](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23696023) (CC-BY-4.0).

- `p142/prepare/`: preparation of the inputs (resampling to 4 mm, liver mask, cropping around the liver).
- `p142/p142_dose_rate_*.json`: one OpenGATE configuration per radionuclide (CT, activity image, radionuclide, 1 MBq, simulation mode).
- `p142/create_benchmark_json.py`: reads the OpenGATE dose-rate images and writes the `p142/p142_*_opengate_benchmark.json` files used on this page.
- `batch_uncertainty.py`: repeats the Lu-177 simulation with different random seeds to measure the uncertainty of the organ mean (`p142/p142_lu177_batch_uncertainty.json`).
- `benchmarks.py`: the cases and acceptance ranges shown above; `test_opengate.py`: the same comparisons as tests; `report.py`: this page.

Each simulation is run with the `opengate_dose_rate` command of OpenGATE, for example:

```bash
opengate_dose_rate p142_dose_rate_lu177.json
```

with `p142_dose_rate_lu177.json`:

```json
{
  "# Input CT image": "",
  "ct_image": "ct_4mm_cropped.nii.gz",
  "table_mat": "Schneider2000MaterialsTable.txt",
  "table_density": "Schneider2000DensitiesTable.txt",
  "density_tolerance_gcm3": 0.2,
  "# Input activity image": "",
  "activity_image": "liver_4mm_cropped.nii.gz",
  "# Input radionuclide": "",
  "radionuclide": "Lu177",
  "# Input total simulated activity in the whole image, in Bq": "",
  "activity_bq": 1e6,
  "# Option: number of threads": "",
  "number_of_threads": 8,
  "# Option: visualisation (for debug)": "",
  "visu": false,
  "# verbosity": "",
  "verbose": true,
  "mode": "vrt",
  "e_factor": 1,
  "output_folder": "output_lu177_vrt"
}
```

To check radot against the stored values, or regenerate this page:

```bash
pytest validation                             # radot vs the stored OpenGATE values
pytest validation --opengate=images           # same, on the real images (downloads the data)
pytest validation --opengate=simulate         # rerun the OpenGATE simulations, then compare
python validation/opengate/report.py          # regenerate this page
```
